integrity: The exact value follows from the established degree-one Gauss image, the explicit cuboctahedral square vertices, and the elementary free-boundary identity equating planar-normal turning with Gauss-map arclength. A small checker verifies only the coordinate arithmetic; it is not used as evidence for the analytic geometric step.
scientific limitations: The theorem concerns the four smooth planar face arcs of the regular-tetrahedron Smyth disk. It does not include corner turning, does not provide a pointwise curvature formula, and makes no claim for arbitrary tetrahedra or for unverified endpoint identifications in a deformation family.
title: Each free-boundary arc of Smyth's regular-tetrahedron disk turns by exactly sixty degrees
